Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 101, verses 1–3:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Qari'ah (The Striking Calamity)

It is Makkiyyah (revealed in Makkah).

The words of the Most High: ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ It is the Resurrection (al-qiyamah), and it was named "al-qari'ah" because it strikes the hearts with terror and severity.

His words ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ are mentioned to express magnification and awe, and likewise ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾.

Almighty God's words: ﴿On the Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾. Al-Farash is the small creatures of living things, such as bedbugs, mosquitoes and locusts, and what gathers around the light of a lamp. Al-mabthuth (scattered): he called it "scattered" because some of it piles upon other parts of it. It was said: some of it mingles into other parts of it. This is like His words: ﴿as if they were scattered locusts﴾. He likened people at the gathering (al-hashr) to it, because some of them mingle into others.

It is his saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool carded﴾, meaning: wool that is fluffed up. Al-ʿihn (the dyed wool) is wool that has been dyed, and it is the most delicate of wool. This is mentioned to convey that the mountains, from the terror of the Day of Resurrection, despite their hardness and strength, become like fluffed-up wool.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 101, verses 6–7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy, then he will be in a pleasant life﴾.

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: meaning, one that is characterized by contentment (rida').

It was also said: pleasing (mardiyya).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 101, verses 6–7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy, then he will be in a pleasant life﴾.

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: meaning, one that is characterized by contentment (rida').

It was also said: pleasing (mardiyya).
And His saying: ﴿But as for him whose scales are light﴾ — in some of the exegetical works it is said that every person has a separate scale for his deeds, of good and of evil.

Ibn al-Sam'ani's Tafsir al-Quran on surah 101, verse 9:

And His saying: ﴿Then his mother is the Abyss (Hawiyah)﴾. That is, his place of return is to the Abyss (al-Hawiyah), and He called it his "mother" because a person takes refuge with his mother; so the Abyss shelters the disbelievers, and it is their mother. And in some reports describing the Fire: "Evil is the mother, and evil is the one who raises (the young)." And it is said: al-Hawiyah is every place into which a person falls and perishes.
And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ The hā' in His saying ﴿what it is﴾ is the hā' of pause (hā' al-waqf) on the fatḥah (the short vowel "a") of the yā'.
"And His saying: ﴿a Fire, blazing fiercely﴾ — meaning: blazing fiercely against the disbelievers, burning them. And Allah knows best."
